rv.q: Humour and pain run alongside one another in this passionately performed revival
The shock of the play, is its warmth, humour and gentle humanity.
A story filled with meaning about the complexities of motherhood, partnership and collective sorrow, The Revlon Girl paints these women with beauty and care.
The cast is one of the strongest I’ve seen at Park Theatre.
The Revlon Girl is an important and perfectly judged work that examines a monumental tragedy with respect, grace, humour and emotional heft.
The Revlon Girl is a powerful piece of drama that respectfully touches on an event that wiped out a generation.
This is a compelling drama that deserves to be seen but as large an audience as possible.

A stirring play and a necessary ode to not only those who were lost, but also those who came together to share their hurt and find community in their healing, The Revlon Girl ’s acclaimed reputation precedes it, and with good reason.

The Revlon Girl is a funny, poignant reminder that small pockets of joy can be found in the darkest of times, and that the greed of faceless corporations causes untold damage to everyday human beings.
This is a moving, beautifully acted and unexpectedly warm piece of theatre, and a fitting tribute in this anniversary year.
The Revlon Girl is an unsentimental examination of how a national tragedy moulds the lives of bereaved mothers.
Maxine Evans's direction of 'The Revlon Girl', revisiting Aberfan sixty years on, is a deeply moving tribute to the grieving mothers of the disaster.
Neil Anthony Docking’s tender, bighearted and surprisingly funny play offers a snapshot of the aftermath of a truly terrible loss.

cn.t: Neil Anthony Docking's play about Aberfan's grieving mothers earns strong praise for its moving, intelligent exploration of trauma. Critics laud its balance of raw emotion with unexpected humor and hope, calling it a breathtaking tribute.
